summary:
# NOTES ON THE FIVE BOOKS (for later lookup; not commentary)

## BOOK 1 — *The Isle of Lies* (M. P. Shiel, 1900s; Gutenberg 77484)

**Frame:** Professor S. S. Reid's diary + letters of Dr. Hannibal-father Lepsius. Chapters I–XV.

**Ch I – The Stele.** Lepsius (c. 45, bachelor, rich, polymath, Hanover Square house) goes to Abyssinia (British mission, 1868, after Magdala). Lake Sana, island monastery; library-mosque on second island. Monks: swaggering monk with two falchions (scarlet morocco scabbards), milder monk. Underground room of dead prior (very old, died before "riches of Jerusalem" inscription); armed gigantic Galla guards coffin. Basalt stele (thumb-thick, ~6 in, copper cap, banyan string) with hieroglyphic/hieratic/demotic. Prior buried with it at 11 pm. Lepsius steals it at night, cuts cords of coffin, coffin slides into lake, he swims (can't swim well), escapes through cocoa-fibre matting, razor slash; nuns' chamber, burning bed; flees in boat past Ethiopian chiefs (dejamatshs). Mission bombarded by priests; three Abyssinians shot. Stele in hand.

**Ch II – Molly O'Hara.** Reid visits Lepsius (who fell ill, went to Galway castle). Stele deciphered except 15 signs / three secret words. Lepsius meets Molly O'Hara (Irish washerwoman, ~25, Southwark, sister a fruit-seller at Ballihooly) on Westminster Bridge, July sun. Tower/Crown Jewels tour. Lepsius's aim: "make a man" through environment-based education (Environment theory; child isolated in a world of gods). He marries Molly (Sept 13, 1869, Lambeth). Lease of island **Shunter** (Outer Hebrides). Son born; Molly dies of milk-fever. Son to be named Hannibal.

**Ch III – The Isle of Lies.** Letters of Lepsius: Hannibal (19 on 21 July) is son raised in isolated delusion on Shunter; Shan Healy (sad "idiot" servant, actually sharp). Race with father over 2 miles, Hannibal always beaten; father's tunnel-trick. Books purged; Peter Pitt invented; Caesar's and Napoleon's defeats hidden. Hannibal knows bombs, runs, languages (never forgets). Lepsius's odd tenderness; Shan boiled-over glass pot; Hannibal beats Shan's head. Moon talk at 3 a.m.; "God made two great lights." Hannibal disappears.

**Ch IV – The Ship.** Hannibal reads stele aloud (fails at "At—"): "Let no man strive to visit them at—"; asks for time on shore. Schooner off Shunter; handkerchief "R. V." found; footprints; bitten chocolate. Lepsius grieves.

**Ch V – "Miss Eve."** Diary of Jeanne Auvache (Frenchwoman, maid to Miss Eve Vickery). Yacht of Mr. Richard Vickery ("Iron King") with daughters Ruth (saint-like, 25) and Eve (21ish, queenly); Lord Astor, Miss Savage, Comte de Courcy (Minister of Interior). Hannibal hides in cabin; Jeanne gagged; he says he knows she's a woman, wants her as wife; name "Hannibal Lepsius"; gives her the stele-stone like ink-bottle.

**Ch VI – The Towers.** Thring railway; Hannibal's wonder at trains; Jeanne says he's French; he hides in river-cave; Jeanne plans marriage licence at St. Arvens.

**Ch VII – The Terraces.** Miss Ruth converts/instructs Hannibal (eyes on Eve); Ruth promises secrecy; Hannibal glorifies stealing; Eve's handkerchief at his ear; Jeanne eavesdrops; Monsieur de Courcy's cane.

**Ch VIII – In the Garden.** Shan Healy arrives; Hannibal beats Monsieur de Courcy's cane aside; Hannibal kisses; Jeanne buys vitriol at Wynton; Ruth betrays him; fire at "Up Brooming" (grocer Perkins). Jeanne asks Nona—she dismisses Jeanne.

**Ch IX – "Vitriolise rai."** Hannibal returns; London escape (Tottenham Court Road, Waterloo Bridge); arrested by Inspector Gibbon and constable Shooter; Hannibal bound them with rope round oak tree; vitriol on shirt sleeves; takes £400 stolen; gives Jeanne note "Beldam Eve, farewell for two years." Jeanne vows to vitriolise him.

**Ch X – "The Moon."** Paris Décavés club gossip: Duc de Rey-Drouilhet, Abbé Sauriau, Isabeau Thiéry, Leflô (Prefect), Saïd Pasha, Reader Meade. Lepsius's moon company, Debenture; public embrace at Quai d'Orsay with Eve; Comte de Courcy plots; Jeanne to be sent to Minister; Hannibal sends stolen money.

**Ch XI – The Chamber-Window.** Shan Healy at Villa des Medicis; telephone whispering-gallery; Ruth, Mr. Vickery, Comtesse de Pichegru-Picard, Mme Grammont; Lepsius's telephone-call; night visit at Eve's window (Mendelssohn Andante); their love dialogue; Eve engaged to de Courcy. Nundcumar (Hindoo, nose-tip burnt by Jeanne's vitriol in Serapis corridor; Lepsius shoots Jeanne, she's taken).

**Ch XII – The Wedding-Place.** Grönland château burnt; wedding moved to Egmond (Brittany). Plot: Lepsius lured to Egmond; Schuré; Château Labîme prison; Brisson of Rouen (false limping Brisson bribes). Abbé Sauriau, Fanny Schuré. Duc gets £20,000 cheque; pill plan.

**Ch XIII – At Egmond.** Summer-house capture; Eve kisses bad Brisson; Lepsius's escape via bombs; carries Eve from burning château over lake; yacht; Nundcumar.

**Ch XIV – At Serapis.** Lepsius's palace Serapis; Miss Eve a prisoner; Healy dying of vitriol; Lepsius's visit to dying Healy; Ruth's reproach; Ruth visits Serapis; Eve on lake.

**Ch XV – To Shunter.** Moon-stock falls; riots; Thiéry's bribe; pills; Thiéry's death; Lepsius blinded by vitriol (by Jeanne, who then attacks Nundcumar's dog Argo). Eve visits; "You should have been good!"; Lepsius and father sail to Shunter; Eve's last words; end.

## BOOK 2 — *Out of the Blue* (Bertrand W. Sinclair; Gutenberg 73542)

Chapters I–XVI. Protagonist **Rock Holloway**, young Texas ranger, sorrel horse **Sangre**; gray Stetson.

- **Ch I (Fort Worth):** Banker **Uncle Bill Sayre** (Trinity Bank; dialect "yo'"), who hires Rock to watch **Buck Walters** (range boss of **Maltese Cross**, estate of dead **Dave Snell**; children Alice and a 16-yr-old boy; Walters co-executor). Advance $500 gold. Maltese Cross on Marias River, Montana. Duffy brothers (Joe, Elmer, Ed, Mark) run **Seventy Seven** herd.
- **Ch II (Odeon, Clark's Ford, Nebraska):** Al Kerr (Capital K, Judith Basin). Mark Duffy assaults Kerr; Rock shoots Mark Duffy dead.
- **Ch III (Steering Wheel):** Rock's trail to Canada/Montana with Steering Wheel outfit under **Dave Wells**; cattle with fresh-burned Steering Wheel brand; Wells' idle crew.
- **Ch IV (Dead Double):** Marias ranch of Nona Parke (TL brand); Doc Martin shot from ambush (lookalike of Rock). Baby **Betty**. Nona hires Rock as "Doc."
- **Ch V (Wrapped in Canvas):** Rock buries Doc in canvas.
- **Ch VI (Very Adroit Rock):** Elmer Duffy believes Rock is Doc. Rock's bluff.
- **Ch VII (Mariners):** Alice Snell; Charlie Shaw (blond TL rider); Buck at White Springs.
- **Ch VIII (Getting Down to Cases):** Doc's saddle with blood; Charlie briefed.
- **Ch IX (Ordered South):** Fort Benton; Walters tells Rock to go south or be killed in 48 hrs.
- **Ch X (Thirty Angry Men):** Alice warns; vigilante posse (Walters, Duffy, 30 riders) to hang Rock; Nona defends; Rock exposes identity; Walters withdraws.
- **Ch XI (Riders on a Rise):** Ambush at ravine; Rock kills Hurley; captures Joe Stack (Texas gunman).
- **Ch XII (Stack Decides to Talk):** Stack confesses ($500 each; Hurley shot Doc). Rock burns foot to extract; releases Stack. Kiss of Nona later.
- **Ch XIII (On the Warpath):** Rock leaves Nona; goes to Capital K; telegram from Sayre "Act on your own judgment."
- **Ch XIV (Hot on the Trail):** Rock with Kerr's men to Sweet Grass Hills; Charlie Shaw leads to hidden corrals.
- **Ch XV (Popping Guns):** Gunfight at East Butte; Charlie shot; Walters charges and is shot by Rock; black horse killed.
- **Ch XVI ("Certainly Not Sad"):** Sayre arrives; Rock offers ledger proof; Nona's kiss: "I'm certainly not sad!"

## BOOK 3 — *Willow the King* (J. C. Snaith; Gutenberg 73075)

Cricket comedy; narrator "I" (Dimsdale, R. C. Richard Cranford Dimsdale, soap-boiler's son). Club: **Little Clumpton** cricket club. Match: Little Clumpton v. **Hickory**, Hickory Park. Team: Captain (Halliday, pipe, "Halliday, have you won the toss?"), Secretary Lawson, Optimist (Brightside), Pessimist (Grimston), Humourist (Merryweather), Worry (Daunton), General Nuisance (Hon. J. Blenkinsop-Comfort), Ancient (Oldknow, 'Notts'), Treasurer. Bowler Billy (drunk). Hickory: Trenthams—A. H. (Archie, Middlesex), H. C. (Charlie, bowler), T. S. M. (Tommy, Harrow), Captain George (Artillery), Grace (Laura Mary, "Grace", twin of Tommy), the Rector (Dr. Trentham), Rev. Elphinstone ("Toddles"), Carteret ("Jimmy", barrister, fat short-slip). Wiggles = ground-man; Biffin = umpire. Ringmaster telephone scorer "the telegraph." Wisden-minded Grace.

**Chapters:** Night before; coming events (lost Authentics cap; Thornhill's cap fetched); match start (wicket dispute: both sides go in—toss farce); Dimsdale is opener, out for 7 l.b.w.; Grace bowls; Dimsdale proposes at Hickory Rectory library; Dimsdale plays first county match (Gloucestershire v Middlesex) — Rectory rules; Grace declares, etc. Ends with marriage notice "Dimsdale–Trentham" in Morning Post.

Key runs: Halliday 204, Oldknow 101, Merryweather 28, Dimsdale 7; Grace bowled Dimsdale in singles; Tonbridge match: T. Trentham selected by telegram "Hooray! Isn't A. J. just a darling!"; Stoddart telegram "If Hawke wants you for India, sing slow. You are going with me."

## BOOK 4 — *A Dead Reckoning* (T. W. Speight; Chambers's Journal 1889)

Nineteen chapters. Clara Brooke (née Danby, b. ~22, bright, impulsive) married to **Gerald Brooke** of Beechley Towers (near London; Polish-raised; excellent pistol-shot; Gerald's cousin **George Crofton**, jilted, dissipated). Aunt **Miss Jane Primby** (spinster, dozes, embroiders). Friend **Lady Fanny Dwyer** (Algy Dwyer). Baron **Otto von Rosenberg** (German ex-diplomat, Beaulieu). Mountebank **Jules Picot** and son **Henri** (blonde, ~8, beautiful). Russian **Karovsky** (Paul Karovsky, Gerald's old Brotherhood acquaintance). Stephanie Lagrange (circus horsewoman, Crofton's later wife; Picot's daughter, sister of Henri). Servants: Bunce (majordomo), Dixon (groom), Margery Shook (girl rescued from canal barge, witch-like laugh, "Muster Geril"). Tom Starkie (friend, red hair; father Sir John Starkie, JP, Penrhyn Court); Roger Chamfrey. Superintendent Drumley of King's Harold police.

**Plot:** Karovsky demands Gerald assassinate Von Rosenberg (who betrayed Polish cell; Karovsky's brother died in mines). Gerald refuses. Von Rosenberg murdered at Beaulieu with Gerald's Indian pistol (lent). Gerald hides in "Priest's Hole" at Penrhyn Court, then as signalman "Maynard" at Cinder Pit Junction (Yorkshire moors); later London Soho lodging No. 5 Pymm's Buildings as "Stewart." Crofton frames/betrays; Picot kills Crofton's (no—Picot rescues; Picot writes confession; Picot shot Von Rosenberg, confesses in court, takes poison in cell). Crofton tries to murder Gerald at Lady Fan's visit; Karovsky/"brotherhood" ends his life. Ending: Gerald and Clara reunited at Towers; Karovsky absolves.

## BOOK 5 — *Shoulder to Shoulder* (Gordon Stables, M.D.; Ward Lock/Shaw)

Narrator: author (grandson) recounting grandfather **Ian (John) Robertson**, Royal Scots 1st Regiment; grandmother **Ellen (Eleanora/Nora)** of Booterstown/Dublin; Auld-da (grandfather) lived in Aberdeenshire ("bonnie Braes of R----"; Bass o' Ury, Inverurie). Plot covers: Culloden story (Fiona, Raoul Dhu, Muirachie the dwarf, Ian's escape, Robertson Robertson's cave, Corney's Cave); school (Dominie Freeschal, tawse, Rachel Freeschal, Tonal/Tom Grahame, kilt-pin fight, Preen Mhor); staymaker in Inverness (Mr. Craig); Cousin Fraser (Captain, Black Watch) enlists John; Fort George; shilling thrown in sea; Captain Drake; O'Reilly; McLeod; Blood; Egypt/Alexandria (Sir Ralph Abercromby); Gibraltar mutiny (Duke of Kent); Dundalk recruiting; marriage to Ellen (Mrs. Stapleton's daughter Eleanor); Peninsula (Corunna, Sir John Moore); Bergen-op-Zoom; Canada/War of 1812; Red-Eye (Micmac friend), daughter Mary rescued from Micmacs; Napoleon exile on St. Helena.
